spec.title: Design docs: the contract/lore split in practice

p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** The genre table says a module contract is binding and a design doc is lore.

p.this-file-is-the-practical-edge: This file is the practical edge: *what spills out* of a contract into a design doc, *what never leaves*, the fork-by-fork shape a design doc uses to record a decision session, the orthogonal-decomposition lesson that makes big designs shippable, and how a design doc grows stale honestly.

split.title: What stays in the contract, what spills out

p.a-contract-is-read-under-time-pressure: A contract is read by an implementer under time pressure.

p.EVERYTHING-IN-A-CONTRACT-MUST-EARN-ITS-P: Everything in it must earn its place.

p.THE-SPLIT-IS-LOAD-BEARING-VERSUS-NARRATI: So the split is not "short versus long" — it is "load-bearing versus narrative".

item.KEEP-THE-DECISION-ITSELF: The **decision itself** — the value, the shape, the chosen option.

item.KEEP-THE-ONE-PARAGRAPH-LOAD-BEARING-WHY: Its **one-paragraph load-bearing why** — the single reason that, if forgotten, would get the decision reverted by accident.

item.KEEP-THE-INVARIANTS: The **invariants** it establishes for everything downstream.

item.SPILL-PRECEDENT-STUDIES: **Precedent studies** — how three other tools solved this, at length. (Contrast with the research genre: research studies an external system for its own sake; a precedent study in a design doc is marshalled to justify *our* choice.)

item.SPILL-FORKS-WEIGHED-AT-LENGTH: **Forks weighed at length** — every option considered, not just the winner.

item.SPILL-PARKED-IDEAS: **Parked ideas** — the "we could later…" branches, explicitly marked as not-yet-decided so no one implements them.

item.SPILL-THE-NARRATIVE-HOW-WE-GOT-HERE: **The narrative "how we got here"** — the path of the discussion, the analogies, the owner's mental model.

p.THE-BOUNDARY-TEST-CONTRACT-SIDE: The test at the boundary: *if deleting this sentence would change what an implementer builds, it is contract.*

p.THE-BOUNDARY-TEST-LORE-SIDE: If deleting it only costs a future reader the story, it is lore.

forks.title: The fork-by-fork decision record

p.FORKS-ARE-THE-MOST-VALUABLE-THING-A-DESI: The most valuable thing a design doc preserves is the set of forks a session resolved — because those are exactly the questions a later session will otherwise re-litigate.

p.RECORD-EACH-FORK-AS-A-FIXED-SKELETON: Record each fork as a fixed skeleton, so the reasoning is scannable rather than buried in prose:

forks.fence:
### Fork N — <the question in one line>
- Options: <A> | <B> | <C> - Chosen: <the winner> - Why: <the deciding reason — a constraint, a cost, a precedent> - Rejected: <A> — because <reason> <C> — because <reason> - Consequence: <what this fork now forces downstream, if anything>

p.two-properties-make-the-shape-pay-off: Two properties make this shape pay off.

p.REJECTED-LINES-ARE-LOAD-BEARING: First, the **Rejected** lines are load-bearing: "we considered X and rejected it because Y" is the single sentence that stops the same X being re-proposed next quarter.

p.A-CONSEQUENCE-SIGNALS-A-TWO-WAY-LINK-CHE: Second, a fork with a **Consequence** that constrains a contract is a signal to check the two-way link — that consequence probably belongs, in one line, at the contract anchor too.

decomposition.title: The orthogonal-decomposition lesson

p.SPLIT-A-LARGE-DESIGN-INTO-INDEPENDENTLY-: When a design is large, the highest-leverage move is usually to split it into **independently-shippable axes that compose** — decisions that have different cost, different dependencies, and can ship as different milestones.

p.why-keeping-the-axes-separate-clarifies: Keeping the axes separate is often the single most clarifying move of a design session: it turns one intimidating change into a short chain where the cheap, independent part ships first and unblocks the rest.

p.worked-sketch-four-axes: A worked sketch. A request to "make the tool multi-package with proper naming" decomposes into four axes:

decomposition.fence: Axis A — Workspace : project = a set of modules | independent → do first Axis B — Selective pub : each module opts in/out | depends on A Axis C — Qualified names: reverse-FQDN identity | depends on the index Axis D — Conflict-aware : collisions fail loudly | depends on C

p.the-finding-decomposition-surfaces: The finding that decomposition surfaces: Axis A alone closes most of the request and depends on nothing, while the expensive part (naming, discovery) is separable and can come later.

p.without-the-split-it-looks-like-a-big-ba: Without the split, the whole thing looks like one big-bang change; with it, the sequencing is obvious.

p.THE-DESIGN-DOC-RECORDS-THE-DECOMPOSITION: The design doc is where this decomposition and its dependency chain are recorded in full; the contract for each axis carries only that axis's decision.

p.A-DESIGN-DOC-RECORDS-WHAT-WAS-TRUE-WHEN-: A design doc records **what was true at the moment it was written**.

p.STALENESS-IS-THE-GENRES-NATURE-NOT-A-FLA: That is not a flaw to be patched away — it is the genre's nature, and pretending otherwise causes more harm than the staleness itself.

item.CORRECTIONS-HAPPEN-ON-CONTRACT-CONFLICT: **Corrections happen on contract conflict.** When the contract moves and the design doc now contradicts it, fix the contradicting passage and note what changed. This is targeted, not cosmetic.

item.WHOLESALE-REWRITES-DO-NOT-HAPPEN: **Wholesale rewrites do not happen** just because time passed. A design doc is not living documentation to be kept current sentence by sentence; that would cost real effort to no benefit and would erase the record of how the thinking actually evolved.

item.A-SUPERSEDED-DESIGN-DOC-IS-ARCHIVED-NOT-: **A superseded design doc is archived, not deleted.** The path from a rejected early design to the shipped one is itself lore the next reader may need.

p.A-DESIGN-DOC-MAY-READ-AS-A-DATED-SNAPSHO: So a design doc is allowed to read as a snapshot with a date on it.

p.IT-MAY-NEVER-DIVERGE-AND-BE-CITED-AS-CUR: What it is never allowed to do is quietly diverge from the contract and then get cited as current — that is the exact failure the precedence law ([`SPEC-GENRES-PROTOCOL.md#precedence`](SPEC-GENRES-PROTOCOL.md#precedence)) exists to prevent.

item.SUM-WHAT-THE-CONTRACT-KEEPS: Contract keeps the decision, its one-paragraph why, constraints, and invariants; everything narrative spills into the design doc.

item.SUM-THE-BOUNDARY-TEST: The boundary test: if deleting a sentence changes what gets built, it is contract; if it only costs the story, it is lore.

item.SUM-RECORD-FORKS-AS-A-SKELETON: Record forks as a fixed skeleton — options, chosen, why, rejected, consequence — so settled questions are not re-litigated.

item.SUM-DECOMPOSE-INTO-COMPOSABLE-AXES: Decompose large designs into independent, composable axes; ship the cheap independent one first.

item.SUM-A-DATED-SNAPSHOT-CORRECTED-ON-CONFLI: A design doc is a dated snapshot; correct it on contract conflict, never rewrite it wholesale to fake currency.
